wrench-lever-arm.alt: A wrench grips a bolt, which is the axis of rotation. A hand pushes on the far end of the handle, a distance r from the axis, with a force F_A at angle θ = 60° to the handle, turning the wrench counterclockwise. A dashed line extends the force’s line of action. The lever arm, r⊥ = r sin θ, is the perpendicular distance from the axis to that line, drawn in amber with a right-angle mark. The panel gives τ = r⊥F = rF sin θ in N·m, notes that a counterclockwise torque is positive, and that a force whose line passes through the axis gives zero torque.
